tier_reason: Tier C stands; caveats corrected: the EPYC leads over randompack (1.26x uniform, 1.03x normal) were measured against randompack's scalar fallback because the CRAN 0.1.10 build never defines BUILD_AVX2, and zurand alone requests 2 MiB pages; the NEON-vs-NEON M1 rows (1.15x uniform, about 1.0x normal) are the fair peer comparison.

corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark workflow against R packages (dqrng, base R, randompack), not std::mt19937, xoshiro or PCG directly; compiler unnamed (EPYC 7763, M1). The x86_64 randompack baseline (CRAN 0.1.10) is built without AVX2, so the EPYC leads (1.26x uniform, 1.03x normal) are over a scalar fallback; on the M1 with NEON on both sides zurand is 1.15x on uniform and 0.97-1.03x on normals. zurand alone requests 2 MiB pages on madvise-mode kernels; threaded rows not like for like; min/max and mean/sd only; 0 stars.

tier_reason: B to C (DASP precedent: harness and correctness evidence): the only numbers are search snippets of the ePrint 2026/947 abstract, and the committed harness compares vectorised SwiftEC hashing against blst's standard SSWU hash and the authors' own scalar SwiftEC signing rather than stock blst, so the speedup is not a like-for-like measurement; the default output is not RFC 9380 interoperable.

corrections.caveats: Repo has bench code and public flags but no numbers; the 'at least 1.57x over blst on an i3-1005G1' claim is a search snippet of ePrint 2026/947 (blocked). The aggregation benches run vendored blst with the standard SSWU hash against *_vec paths using the cheaper SwiftEC hash (SWIFTEC_ON 1), and the sign rows compare the authors' scalar SwiftEC code, not stock blst; default SwiftEC signatures are not RFC 9380 interoperable. Reuses the catalogued avxbls pairing code; self-tests never fail on bad signatures.
